name: Pet Moving Checklist
description: An owner-focused checklist for moving house with a pet, covering records, ID, travel and settling in.

items.text: Request copies of your pet's full medical records
Confirm vaccinations are current
Ask your vet about travel, sedation or motion sickness
items.note: Never give human medication without veterinary advice

items.text: Refill any ongoing medications before the move
Research a new vet near your future home
Update your microchip registration with the new address and phone
Replace ID tags with current contact details
Update any pet license or registration with local authorities
Take a recent photo in case your pet goes missing during the move
Acclimate your pet to the carrier or crate in advance
Pack a travel kit with food, water, bowls and waste bags
Plan rest, water and bathroom stops for long drives
Confirm airline or transport rules if flying or shipping the pet
Never leave a pet alone in a parked vehicle
Confine your pet to a closed, quiet room or arrange boarding
Place a clear sign on the door so movers keep it shut
Keep collar and ID tags on the pet at all times
Pack a familiar blanket, bed or toy to bring on the journey
Feed lightly before travel to reduce nausea
Set up one secured, quiet room with familiar items first
Pet-proof the home and check for escape routes and hazards
Introduce the rest of the home gradually
Keep feeding, walk and sleep routines consistent
Update walking routes and locate the nearest emergency vet

faq.q: How do I prepare my pet for a house move?
faq.a: Update ID and microchip details, gather vet records, keep your pet's routine steady, pack a travel kit, and set up a quiet, secured room in the new home before the move so they have a calm base.

faq.q: How do I keep my pet safe on moving day?
faq.a: Confine the pet to a closed, quiet room or board them for the day so open doors and movers don't cause an escape. Make sure they wear a collar with current ID tags throughout.

faq.q: Should I see a vet before moving with a pet?
faq.a: Yes. Ask your veterinarian for copies of records, ensure vaccinations are current, request advice on travel and motion sickness, and ask about requirements if moving to a new region or country.

faq.q: How long does it take a pet to settle after a move?
faq.a: Many pets need days to a few weeks to adjust. Keep routines consistent, give them a familiar-smelling safe space, and watch for changes in eating or behavior, consulting a vet if concerns persist.

faq.q: Can I print this pet moving checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can carry it through the move and check off each task as you go.
